text: Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!

speaker: King Saul
text: You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.

text: The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.

speaker: David
text: I cannot walk in these, | I am not accustomed to them.

speaker: David
text: I need stones for my sling. Come with me to the brook!

speaker: Shammah
text: I am Shammah. Third of eight brothers!

text: Do not go near the valley.

text: My knees have not stopped shaking all week.

speaker: Soldier
text: Every morning. Every evening. He just keeps coming.

speaker: Soldier
text: Riches or no riches, I am staying right here by the fire.

speaker: Soldier
text: Did you see that? One stone!

speaker: Soldier
text: One scratch on this post for every day he has come out.

About 9 feet 9 inches. Taller than a doorway!

speaker: Soldier
text: To the man who kills him the king will give great riches.

About 125 pounds, just for the coat.

text: Thank Jesse for the cheese. You know what the giant is offering?

About 15 pounds, just for the point. You can barely lift one of these!
You scramble up the rock. From here you can see everything.
The Philistines stood on one hill and the Israelites stood on another, with the valley between them.
The king's own armor. Better not touch it.
You lift King Saul's bronze helmet onto your head. It slides right down over your eyes.
Way too big. You put it back before anyone sees.

speaker: Cook
text: Hands full? Come back when they are empty.

speaker: Cook
text: The men at the front have stood in the sun for forty days. Take this water to three of them.

speaker: Cook
text: Three soldiers at the front. Go on!

speaker: Cook
text: Thank you. They will not say so, but that water mattered.

speaker: Cook
text: Nobody is thirsty now. Listen to them shout!

text: Thank you. I have not slept. Every time I close my eyes, I see him.

speaker: Soldier
text: I keep thinking someone braver will go. Then I remember everyone is thinking that.

text: If our champion loses, we all become servants. Who would risk that?

speaker: Soldier
text: I keep hearing bleating behind the tents. Would you go and look?
A lamb! It must have followed David all the way from Bethlehem.

speaker: Soldier
text: So that is what I heard! One of Jesse's, I would bet. Keep it close until David can take it home.
